newsitem.title: USA: Iraqi oil contract squeaks through on U.N. limit.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi oil contract squeaks through on U.N. limit.

text.p: The United Nations overseers have squeaked in another Iraq oil contract in just under the limit to the "oil-for-food" deal, U.N. officials said on Friday
The spot deal for 360,000 barrels puts overall oil sales at 121.56 million barrels, giving an estimated value very near the accord's $2.142 billion ceiling.
U.N. officials could provide no more details on the 51st contract and stated that changing oil prices may or may not allow a small number of additional spot sales.
Iraq's agreement with the U.N. expires June 7, after running 180 days from the deal's inception on December 10.
Terms of the accord allow Baghdad to sell $2 billion over the six months and will be reviewed for renewal by the Security Council before it expires.

Receipt limits are actually pegged above $2 billion in order to compensate Turkey for pipeline fees, and includes a rollover from the first 90 days of the accord when sales did not quite reach the proscribed $1.07 billion limit.
Nearly two-thirds of oil proceeds are earmarked for food and medicine purchases, as part of a humanitarian exception to sanctions placed on Iraq after it invaded Kuwait in 1990.

Before June 7, U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan is to issue a report on the accord's effectiveness in alleviating suffering in the country, within a broad progress report on the deal's implementation.
The U.N. Security Council was then to take action on renewing the accord.
